title: Two Parts of a Complex Number Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Room 3 is only half an address: you also need the floor. Diya waited in room 3 on the second floor while her friend waited in room 3 on the ground floor. Complex numbers work the same way: one number, two separate parts. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) we learn to read both parts.

You will see the NCERT definition z = a + ib with Re z = a and Im z = b, move a point live on a two-part address board as a and b change, compare purely real and purely imaginary numbers side by side, tidy an untidy number into a + ib before reading its parts, and slide k live to find when (k - 2) + (k² - 9)i is purely real or purely imaginary. A pause-and-think question, the exam trap about Im(3 - 4i), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:
0:00 Room 3, but which floor?
0:31 Definition: z = a + ib, Re z and Im z
1:03 Live: the two-part address board
1:33 Purely real vs purely imaginary
2:13 Tidy first, then read the parts
2:47 Worked example: slide k
3:38 Exam trap: Im(3 - 4i) is -4
3:54 Where it is asked
4:06 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:46 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 40): Algebra of Complex Numbers. Two moves on a map: we add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers.
